tasks.title: LVM board: from disks to a volume and its growth
tasks.statement: Build a server's storage the way an administrator does: disks, physical volumes (pvcreate), a volume group (vgextend), logical volumes (lvcreate) and filesystems. The board counts the extents itself: a physical volume is a little smaller than its disk (the first megabyte holds metadata), a volume takes a whole number of extents, and the filesystem has to grow together with the volume (lvextend -r). Four scenarios: build a volume from two disks, extend a volume, add a disk to a full group, and find the physical volume that was never added to the group. The exercise is solved when all scenarios are solved.
tasks.hint: Select an object and read its status and the reason on the right. Free space is counted in extents of the group: a 50 GiB volume does not fit on a single 50 GiB disk. If you grew the volume, grow the filesystem too.

tasks.title: LVM board: evacuate a disk, mirrors, VM disks
tasks.statement: The same objects, but the questions are about failure and replacement. Four scenarios: free a physical volume for pvmove (is there room on the others), a mirrored volume that survives the loss of any disk, VM disks in the volume group of a block domain (every VM disk is a logical volume), and retiring an old disk. The exercise is solved when all scenarios are solved.
tasks.hint: The data of a physical volume can be moved only if the other physical volumes of the group have enough free extents. A mirror copy lives on a separate physical volume, so a mirror needs two physical volumes in the group.

tasks.title: Volume size in extents
tasks.statement: The lvcreate -L option takes a size as a number with an optional unit. Input units are always binary and the case does not matter: b is bytes, s is 512-byte sectors, k is KiB, m is MiB, g is GiB, t is TiB; with no unit the number means mebibytes. The number may be fractional, for example 1.5g. A volume's size is a multiple of the physical extent, and the requested size is rounded up to a whole number of extents. Write a function lv_extents(pe_kib, size): pe_kib is the extent size in KiB, size is a string such as "10G", "512k" or "1.5g". Return a tuple (number of extents, resulting size in KiB). A zero size gives (0, 0).
tasks.hint: Multiply the number by the unit's factor in KiB (use Fraction to stay exact) and divide by the extent, rounding up.

tasks.title: Percentages in -l: down or up
tasks.statement: The -l option takes a percentage of the VG, of the group's free space (FREE), of the free space of the listed PVs (PVS) or, for lvextend, of the volume itself (LV). The percentage is computed in integers, extents n = pct * base // 100, rounded as follows: lvcreate always rounds down; lvextend/lvreduce (cmd = "resize") round up, that is n = (pct * base + 99) // 100, except with a minus sign, where they round down. The base: VG is all the group's extents vg_pe, FREE is the free free_pe, PVS is pvs_free_pe, the free extents of the listed PVs, and if no PV is listed in the command (pvs_free_pe is None) it is vg_pe; LV is the volume's lv_pe extents. Limits: with cmd = "create" a percentage of VG is at most free_pe, and the base LV is invalid (return 0); with cmd = "resize", sign "" (an absolute size) and base VG the result is at most lv_pe + free_pe. Write a function percent_extents(cmd, sign, pct, base, vg_pe, free_pe, pvs_free_pe, lv_pe): cmd is "create" or "resize", sign is "", "+" or "-", base is "VG", "FREE", "PVS" or "LV", pct is an integer. Return the number of extents.
tasks.hint: First pick the base, then the rounding (up = cmd == "resize" and sign != "-"), then apply the two limits.

tasks.title: A script of LVM commands on a VG model
tasks.statement: The group model: the extent is pe_kib KiB; a PV of S MiB gives (S - 1) * 1024 // pe_kib usable extents (the first MiB holds the label and metadata); pvs is a dictionary PV name → size in MiB. Logical volumes are linear, a volume's size is a number of extents, and the free total is "the group's extents minus the sum of the volumes' extents". Write a function run_script(pe_kib, pvs, commands): commands is a list of strings executed in order, each producing a result from the list below. The commands: "lvcreate -n NAME -L SIZE" or "lvcreate -n NAME -l SPEC"; "lvextend -L SIZE LV" or "lvextend -l SPEC LV"; "lvreduce -L SIZE LV"; "lvremove LV"; "vgextend PVNAME SIZE_MIB" (always "ok", adds the usable extents of the new PV). SIZE is as in lvcreate -L: a number with a unit b/s/k/m/g/t, binary, MiB when there is none, case-insensitive; for lvextend and lvreduce a leading plus or minus makes it an increment. SPEC is an integer number of extents or N%FREE, N%VG (lvextend also takes N%LV); with lvextend a leading plus means an increment. Rounding: an absolute size, and an increment when growing, round up to the extent; the increment in lvreduce -L -SIZE rounds down (at most the requested amount is removed); percentages follow the previous task (lvcreate rounds down and %VG is at most the free space; lvextend rounds up and an absolute %VG is at most current size + free; lvreduce takes only -L). Results: "ok"; "unchanged" (the new size equals the current one); "error: exists" (the name is taken), "error: not found" (no such volume), "error: zero size" (lvcreate gave 0 extents or lvreduce gave a size of 0 or less), "error: no space" (not enough free extents), "error: not larger" (lvextend asked for less than the current size), "error: not smaller" (lvreduce asked for more than the current size). Checks go in this order: name, then size, then space. An error leaves the model unchanged. Return a tuple (list of results, dictionary volume → size in KiB, number of free extents at the end).
tasks.hint: Keep a dictionary volume → extents and recompute the free total before each command; compute the number of extents first, then compare.

tasks.title: What we lose if a disk dies
tasks.statement: You get the output of lvs -a -o lv_name,vg_name,lv_attr,lv_size,pool_lv,origin,devices (headers LV VG Attr LSize Pool Origin Devices). The columns are aligned by the header: a column's value starts no further left than the first character of its header and ends before the start of the next one; empty cells are spaces (cut the columns by header positions, not by spaces). The function failure_impact(text, pv) returns a sorted list of the names of the visible volumes (names not in square brackets) that are lost if the disk pv fails, for example "/dev/sdb". The Devices column is a comma-separated list like path(extent number); count only the items that start with /dev/, the others (volume names) take no part. Rules. 1) A visible volume with extents on pv is lost. 2) A hidden volume in square brackets belongs to the parent whose name is the hidden name without the suffix _tdata, _tmeta, _rimage_N, _mimage_N, _rmeta_N, _mlog or _pmspare. Extents of a hidden _tdata or _tmeta volume on pv doom the parent (a thin pool). Hidden _rmeta_N, _mlog and _pmspare are ignored. 3) If the parent has hidden copies _rimage_N or _mimage_N, it is lost only if every copy has extents on pv (otherwise it survives, degraded). 4) A thin volume (the first Attr character is V) is lost if the pool named in the Pool column is lost. 5) A classic snapshot (the first Attr character is s) is lost if the volume in the Origin column is lost; losing a snapshot does not affect its origin. Rules 4 and 5 also apply along chains of dependencies.
tasks.hint: Take the column positions from the first line with re.finditer(r'\S+', ...); then map hidden volumes to their parents and keep adding dependent volumes while the set grows.

tasks.title: Problems in an lvs --reportformat json report
tasks.statement: You get the output of lvs --reportformat json -o lv_name,vg_name,lv_attr,lv_size,pool_lv,origin,data_percent,metadata_percent as text: an object with the key "report", holding a list of reports, each with a list "lv" of objects with string values (percentages are strings like "41.20", an empty string means no value). Write a function lvs_problems(text, limit) that finds the problem volumes and returns a list of strings like "vg/lv:problem". Skip volumes whose name is in square brackets. The characters of lv_attr are numbered from 0. The problems: invalid — character 4 is I or S; merge-failed — character 4 is m or M; check-needed — character 4 is c or C; out-of-data — character 0 is t and character 8 is D; meta-readonly — character 0 is t and character 8 is M; failed — character 8 is F; partial — character 8 is p; data-high — character 0 is t and data_percent >= limit; meta-high — character 0 is t and metadata_percent >= limit; snapshot-high — character 0 is s and data_percent >= limit. A volume may have several problems. Sort the result by group, then by volume name, then by the problem's order in this list. An empty report gives an empty list.
tasks.hint: json.loads, then two nested loops over report and lv; convert percentages to float only when the string is not empty.

tasks.title: A thin pool: writes, trim and autoextend
tasks.statement: A model of a thin pool (everything in MiB). The pool has pool_mib of data; thin is a dictionary thin volume → virtual size. Nothing is written at first, so each volume uses 0. Events in order: ["write", volume, mib] — write mib MiB into not-yet-allocated blocks of the volume: min(mib, virtual size − already allocated) is wanted, and no more than the pool's free space is allocated; if less than wanted was allocated the result is "full" (the write did not finish, everything that was left is taken), otherwise "ok"; ["trim", volume, mib] — free at most mib MiB of the volume (result "ok"); ["extend", mib] — grow the pool by mib (result "extended"). After each event autoextend runs if the threshold is below 100: when the pool's used space is strictly greater than the threshold percent of the pool size, the pool grows by pool_mib * percent // 100 (once per event) and a result "ok" becomes "autoext" ("full" and "extended" stay). A threshold below 50 counts as 50; a threshold of 100 or more turns autoextend off. Write a function thin_timeline(pool_mib, thin, events, autoext): autoext is a pair [threshold, percent]. Return a tuple (pool size at the end, used at the end, Data% at the end rounded to two decimals with round(used * 100 / pool, 2), list of event results).
tasks.hint: Keep the allocated amount per thin volume; the pool's used space is the sum. Compare to the threshold in integers: used * 100 > threshold * pool.

tasks.title: A classic snapshot: filling up and going invalid
tasks.statement: A model of a classic (copy-on-write) snapshot. The origin volume of origin_mib MiB is divided into chunks of chunk_kib KiB (origin_mib * 1024 is divisible by chunk_kib); the snapshot area holds cap = snap_mib * 1024 // chunk_kib chunks, but not more than the number of chunks in the origin (there is nothing more to copy). A write [start, length] (KiB, length > 0) touches the chunks numbered from start // chunk_kib to (start + length − 1) // chunk_kib, but not past the end of the origin; each touched chunk is copied into the snapshot area on its first write (a repeated write to the same chunk is free). If there is not enough room for the copies, as many chunks as fit are copied in order of their numbers, the snapshot becomes invalid on that write, and all later writes change nothing. Autoextend: after each write, if the snapshot has not gone invalid and the threshold is below 100, then when strictly more than the threshold percent of the area is full, the area grows by cap * percent // 100 chunks (not beyond the origin's chunk count); a threshold below 50 counts as 50. Write a function snap_timeline(origin_mib, snap_mib, chunk_kib, writes, autoext): autoext is a pair [threshold, percent]. Return a tuple (the snapshot is still valid: True/False, chunks copied, the area's capacity in chunks at the end, the index (from 0) of the first write that invalidated the snapshot, or -1).
tasks.hint: Keep a set of already copied chunks; for each write take the new chunks and compare their count with the free room.

tasks.title: A plan to retire a disk from a group
tasks.statement: You get the output of pvs -o pv_name,vg_name,pv_pe_count,pv_pe_alloc_count: the first line is a header, then one line per PV with the columns PV name, group, total extents, allocated extents. A PV that belongs to no group has an empty group cell, and its line has only three fields. Write a function evacuate_plan(text, pv): the list of commands that retire pv from its group. If pv is not in the output, return ["error: unknown PV"]; if pv is in no group, ["error: not in a VG"]; if its group has no other PV, ["error: last PV of the VG"]. If pv has no allocated extents, two commands are needed: "vgreduce GROUP PV", "pvremove PV". Otherwise pvmove moves pv's allocated extents to the free extents of the other PVs of the same group (PVs of other groups and PVs in no group do not count): if they suffice, the three commands "pvmove PV", "vgreduce GROUP PV", "pvremove PV"; if not, ["error: short by N extents"], where N is how many extents are missing.
tasks.hint: Lines with three fields are PVs with no group; the free space of the other PVs in the group is total minus allocated.

tasks.title: Placing volumes on disks: linear, striped, mirrored
tasks.statement: A placement model. free is a dictionary PV name → free extents. The function alloc_plan(free, kind, n, extents) returns a dictionary PV → how many extents to take on it (zeros left out) or an error string. kind "linear": extents are taken from the PVs in alphabetical order of their names, as much as each has, until extents are gathered; n is ignored; if the total free is smaller, return "error: not enough free extents". kind "striped": n stripes, the number of extents is rounded up to a multiple of n, and each stripe takes extents_rounded // n extents on a separate PV. kind "raid1": n copies of extents extents each, every copy on a separate PV (the small metadata volumes are ignored). For striped and raid1 choose, among the PVs whose free space is at least the amount needed on one PV, the n PVs with the most free space (ties by name); if fewer than n such PVs exist, return "error: not enough PVs with free space".
tasks.hint: For striped and raid1 first compute "needed on one PV", filter the PVs and sort by (-free, name).

tasks.title: A device-mapper name
tasks.statement: LVM builds the names in /dev/mapper: the group, the volume and an optional internal layer are joined by a single hyphen, and every hyphen inside a group or volume name is doubled. For example, the group my-vg and the volume web-1 give "my--vg-web--1", and the cow layer of the snapshot snap in the group vg0 gives "vg0-snap-cow". Write a function split_dm_name(name) that returns a tuple (group, volume, layer); the layer is an empty string when there is none. Parse from left to right: a pair "--" is one hyphen inside a name, a single hyphen is the boundary between parts. If there are neither two nor three parts (for example the name has no boundary, or too many), return ("", "", "").
tasks.hint: Walk the characters: at a hyphen look at the next one: if it is a hyphen too, append one hyphen to the current part and skip both, otherwise start a new part.
